findings.title: Resource lookup uses ResourceServer ID instead of clientId as owner, so per-client permissions are never found
findings.body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` (line 214) and `hasPermission(String)` (line 244), `resourceStore.findByName(server, ..., server.getId())` passes `server.getId()` (a UUID) as the `ownerId` parameter. However, when resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (line 104: `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())`) and `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` (via `RepresentationToModel`, which defaults the owner to `resourceServer.getClientId()`), the resource owner is set to `server.getClientId()` (`"admin-permissions"`), not `server.getId()`. As a result, `resourceStore.findByName(server, ..., server.getId())` always returns `null`: `hasPermission(String)` always returns `false`, and `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` never finds the specific client resource and always falls back to the all-clients resource (ignoring per-client permissions whenever an all-clients policy exists, or failing when none exists). Use `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId())` (which defaults to `server.getClientId()`) and `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`, matching `UserPermissionsV2`.

findings.title: Per-client authorization resources created without setting resource type, breaking getClientsWithPermission
findings.body: `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission` (line 138) queries `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`. However, when per-client (or per-user) resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (line 104), `resource.setType(resourceType)` is never called—only the `"Clients"` all-resource created in `init()` has its type set. Consequently, `findByType` only ever visits the `"Clients"` resource type resource (whose name is `"Clients"`, not a client UUID) and never returns any individual client IDs for which the caller has permission. (And in `PermissionClientTest.testManageOnlyOneClient`, `findAll()` only returned 1 client because `myclient` happened to have `view` scope on the `"Clients"` or other path, or because `getClientsWithPermission` wasn't the path that matched).

findings.title: canView() does not return true when caller has MANAGE permission on all clients
findings.body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.canView()` (line 87), it checks `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` (or `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`). When a user is granted the `manage` scope on all clients (`Clients` resource) without the `view` scope, `canManage()` returns `true`, but `canView()` returns `false` because `canViewClientDefault()` only checks admin roles (`VIEW_CLIENTS`, `MANAGE_CLIENTS`) and `hasPermission(VIEW)` only checks for the `view` scope. Since `canList()` delegates to `canView()`, and `ClientsResource.getClients()` checks `auth.clients().canView()`, an admin with `manage` permission on all clients will not have general view access (e.g., `canView()` is false, and in `testManageAllClients` listing only works if `getSearchableClients` happens to match the `"Clients"` resource). `canView()` should also return `true` when `canManage()` is `true` (or pass both `VIEW` and `MANAGE` scopes to `hasPermission`, as `canView(ClientScopeModel)` does on line 121).

findings.title: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName does not handle CLIENTS resource type
findings.body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` (lines 304-326) resolves human-readable resource names when converting policies/permissions to representations (used by the Admin UI when listing resources attached to a permission). It currently only handles `USERS.getType()` and falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()` (which is `null` for auto-created client resources) for `CLIENTS.getType()`. It should also handle `CLIENTS.getType()` (returning e.g. `"All clients"` for `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` and `client.getClientId()` when looking up by `resource.getName()`).

findings.title: All-clients permission is not evaluated as a fallback when a per-client resource exists for a different scope
findings.body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` (lines 214-224), the all-clients resource (`AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE`) is only loaded if `resource == null` (i.e., no resource exists for that specific client). If a specific permission was created for `clientA` with only scope `configure` (creating the resource for `clientA`), and an all-clients permission was also created granting `manage` (or `map-roles`), evaluating `hasPermission(clientA, MANAGE)` will find `clientA`'s resource, evaluate only the policies attached to `clientA`, see that `manage` is not granted there, and return `false` without ever evaluating the all-clients permission (unlike `UserPermissionsV2`, which passes both the specific resource and the resource-type resource, or falls back when the scope is not granted).
